question: For users who obtained badges between 2010 and 2014, identify those whose posts have received comments. Calculate the total number of posts they created, count how many of their posts are well-finished, and list their display names along with their reputation. Group results by user and filter to show only users who have created at least 1 post and have a reputation greater than 100. Also include a status indicator showing whether each user is from New York or not.

prediction.sql:
SELECT
    u."XCL_055" AS display_name,
    u."XCL_053" AS reputation,
    COUNT(p."XCL_026") AS total_posts,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p."XCL_038" > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS well_finished_posts,
    CASE WHEN u."XCL_058" LIKE '%New York%' THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS is_from_new_york
FROM users u
JOIN badges b ON u."XCL_052" = b."XCL_002"
JOIN posts p ON u."XCL_052" = p."XCL_033"
JOIN comments c ON p."XCL_026" = c."XCL_006"
WHERE b."XCL_004" BETWEEN '2010-01-01' AND '2014-12-31'
GROUP BY u."XCL_052"
HAVING COUNT(p."XCL_026") >= 1 AND u."XCL_053" > 100

scope_review.reason: No semantic correction is required. The submitted SQL correctly identifies users with badges between 2010 and 2014, filters to those whose posts have comments (via the join to comments), and aggregates post counts and 'well-finished' post counts (defined as posts with comment_count > 0). The reputation filter uses the correct column (users.XCL_053) and the location check uses the correct column (users.XCL_058). The grain validation shows repeated post keys, which is expected because the join to comments creates multiple rows per post; however, since the aggregates are COUNT(post_id) and SUM(CASE...), and the question asks for the count of posts, the current logic effectively counts the number of comment-post pairs. Wait, if a post has 5 comments, it will be counted 5 times in COUNT(p.XCL_026). The question asks for 'total number of posts they created'. This implies distinct posts. The current SQL counts post-comment pairs. I should use COUNT(DISTINCT p."XCL_026") to ensure each post is counted once, regardless of how many comments it has. Similarly for well-finished posts, if a post has comments, it is well-finished. If it has 5 comments, it should be counted once. So SUM(CASE WHEN p."XCL_038" > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) would also be inflated by the number of comments. I need to count distinct posts that satisfy the condition. Let's fix the aggregation to use DISTINCT.

SUM(CASE WHEN p.XCL_038 > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) also sums over duplicated rows, inflating the count of well-finished posts.
To correctly count 'total number of posts' and 'how many of their posts are well-finished', the aggregation must operate on distinct post identifiers.
The eligibility condition 'posts have received comments' is satisfied by the existence of a join to comments, but the measure should be the count of unique posts.
